# Temple Scroll Column 33 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 33 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 33:1 — "stoas" vs. "covered walkways" — architectural terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "stoas" | Preserves Hellenistic architectural term used in scholarship |
| LOGOS | "stoas" | Same — standard in DSS studies |
| PNEUMA | "covered walkways" | Functional description accessible to general readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "stoas" per EMET and LOGOS. The term is established in biblical archaeology and Dead Sea Scrolls scholarship.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 33:4 — "chambers" vs. "dining halls" — room function

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "chambers" | General term; function specified in context |
| LOGOS | "chambers" | Same formal term |
| PNEUMA | "dining halls" | Specifies function directly in the noun |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "chambers" per EMET and LOGOS. The Hebrew uses a general term for rooms; the eating function is stated in the following verse.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 33:5 — "peace offerings" vs. "fellowship offerings" — shelamim rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "peace offerings" | Traditional rendering of shelamim |
| LOGOS | "peace offerings" | Same traditional term |
| PNEUMA | "fellowship offerings" | Emphasizes communal aspect of the sacrifice |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "peace offerings" per EMET and LOGOS. Consistent with project convention established in Leviticus (shelamim = "peace offerings").

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 33:7 — "appointed feasts" vs. "appointed festivals" vs. "appointed feasts" — mo'adim rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "appointed feasts" | Traditional rendering of mo'adim |
| LOGOS | "appointed festivals" | Slightly more formal variant |
| PNEUMA | "appointed feasts" | Same as EMET |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "appointed feasts" per EMET and PNEUMA majority. "Feasts" better captures the eating context of the surrounding verses.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/PNEUMA.

---

## 33:14 — "sons of Israel" vs. "Israelites" vs. "ordinary Israelites" — lay designation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the sons of Israel" | Literal bene yisrael |
| LOGOS | "the Israelites" | Standard English equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "ordinary Israelites" | Adds "ordinary" to contrast with priests and Levites |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET rendering: "the sons of Israel." The literal form preserves the Hebrew patronymic, and the contrast with priests and Levites is clear from context without adding "ordinary."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 33:16 — "they are holy" vs. "each group is holy" vs. "each group has its own sacred standing" — holiness phrasing

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "for they are holy, each man in his place" | Literal with individual focus |
| LOGOS | "for each group is holy, each in its appointed place" | Group-level holiness language |
| PNEUMA | "for each group has its own sacred standing and its own designated place" | Explanatory paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted compromise: "for they are holy, each in his appointed place." Uses EMET's literal subject ("they") with LOGOS's "appointed place."

**Status:** Resolved as compromise.

---
